701306.t: It has been proposed to derive from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʷs-ih₂-, citing cognates such as Latin ascia and a number of Germanic words, such as Old English æx (English axe).

701308.t: According to some scholars, from ἄγω (ágō, “to lead, draw out or down”) + -τιος (-tios) (perhaps via an unattested intermediate ἄξις (áxis, “weight”)), with sense development "draw down (in the scale)" > "weigh, import".

701310.t: From ἀξιόω (axióō, “to think or deem worthy”) + -μα (-ma).

701318.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ὁρατός (horātós, “seen”), verbal adjective of ὁράω (horáō).

701300.t: From ἀν- (an-, “without”) + ὄνυμα (ónuma, Aeolic dialectal form of ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”)) + -ος (-os, adjective-forming suffix).

701381.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + πεῖρα (peîra, “trial, attempt”) + -ος (-os). Compare with Latin peritus.

701330.t: From ἀπο- (ăpo-, “from, back”) + αἰτέω (aitéō, “to ask, beg”).

701312.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aksōn, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs-. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀰𐀚 (a-ko-so-ne), Sanskrit अक्ष (akṣa, “axle, axis, balance beam”) and Latin axis.

701350.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sm̥-, zero-grade of *sem- (“one”). The second part is obscure, but the word may be some syncope of *ἁ-πακυς, from Proto-Indo-European *sm̥-pn̥kʷu- (“(lit.) all-one”).

701303.t: From ἀν- (an-, “not”) + ὄφελος (óphelos, “advantage, help”) + -ης (-ēs, adjective suffix).

701336.t: Unknown, though of similar formation to ὁμαλός (homălós, “even, level”) and ἀταλός (atălós, “tender, shaking”). Possibly related to ἅπτω (hắptō, “to touch”).

701375.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂pelH- (“to speak publicly”), and related via this root to Latvian pel̂t (“to revile”).

701351.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + παραιτέομαι (păraitéomai, “to beg, entreat”) + -τος (-tos).
